title: Domain-Specific Protocol Orchestration
business: Financial firms managing complex, high-frequency regulatory reporting pipelines.
problem: Engineers struggle with boilerplate code when mapping diverse, evolving financial data formats to rigid internal reporting schemas, leading to maintenance bottlenecks.
solution: Racket allows developers to create a domain-specific language (DSL) via macros that abstracts away the repetitive mapping logic, enabling domain experts to define reporting rules in a syntax tailored to their specific data structures.
steps: Define the core syntax rules using Racket's macro system to map domain-specific keywords to underlying Racket functions.
Implement a parser to handle the specific surface syntax of the financial reporting rules.
Integrate the macro-based DSL into the existing Racket project without requiring external build tools.
Utilize DrRacket's IDE support to provide visual feedback and identifier tracking for the new language constructs.
outcome: Reduced code duplication and improved clarity in reporting logic, allowing developers to focus on business rules rather than syntactic boilerplate.
limitation: The primary trade-off is the cognitive overhead of mastering the macro system; developers must verify that their custom syntax correctly propagates source information to ensure the IDE remains useful for debugging.

code.content:
(define-syntax (report-rule stx) ;; Define a macro to simplify reporting logic
  (syntax-parse stx
    [(_ field value) #'(set-field! field value)])) ;; Rewrite custom syntax to standard Racket
code.explanation: This macro maps a domain-specific 'report-rule' command directly to the underlying field-setting function, reducing boilerplate in the financial pipeline.
